correctness.rationale: For every sufficiently small positive intensity ratio, exact differentiation of the two-species Poisson richness produces H=SP-x(SQ+P^2); its rewritten exponential sign identity is verified symbolically and numerically. Uniform bounds exclude roots outside two C1-controlled crossover windows. The first root lies at L+log L+o(1) and has slope ε(L+log L+1+o(1)); the second occurs at y*/ε+o(1/ε) with limiting slope 1-y*. The bracket 2(1-y)-exp(-y) has exactly one positive root because its derivative is exp(-y)-2<0. Numerical checking independently tested 2000 algebraic instances and five two-extremum scenarios. No claim depends on a finite search.

The new, more precise claim is the exactly-two-extrema theorem for the homogeneous continuous Poisson rare-species limit and two explicit, sharply separated asymptotic scales and heights. value.rationale: The local species–area exponent is used to interpret diversity across scales, and a common species plus an exceptionally rare one is the smallest nontrivial ecological abundance contrast. The theorem excludes all additional scale transitions for sufficiently large contrast and quantifies a double-log survey area where the exponent bottoms out, a distinct inverse-intensity secondary peak scale, and a nonzero universal late-peak height. These are structural quantitative statements absent from a generic curvature illustration; finite computation alone is not the value claim.
